behaviours.description: Compares each string's maximum and minimum cell voltage against three nested over- and under-voltage tiers and raises the matching diagnosis entry on each tier, clearing the tiers the value has returned inside.
Raises an additional deep-discharge diagnosis when the undervoltage-MSL handler reports an error and the minimum voltage is also at or below the deep-discharge threshold.
Selects between the discharge and the charge temperature tier sets from the sign of the string current, so the applicable limit depends on current direction rather than on mode alone.
Skips a string's current comparison entirely when the database marks that string current invalid, so an untrusted measurement does not raise a limit diagnosis.
Compares absolute string current against direction-specific string and cell current limits and against the pack current limit, raising the charge or discharge entry accordingly.
Detects a measured current on a string whose contactors are open, which is the condition the fuse and the open-sense wiring are expected to make impossible.
The diagnosis handler every SOA check calls into; it applies the configured per-entry occurrence threshold and delay and is what actually makes a raised entry active.

concurrency_and_isr_context.shared_state: None in this module: the four functions hold no static state and write only through DIAG_Handler and the caller-supplied structures. The call site is BMS_Trigger (bms.c:898-1691), which invokes SOA_CheckVoltages, SOA_CheckTemperatures, SOA_CheckCurrent and SOA_CheckSlaveTemperatures in that order at bms.c:913-917, before the BMS state machine's own re-entrance guard at bms.c:920.

guard.statement: This record says where the SOA comparison code is and what it does, including the parts of FB2-SW-DSN-000002 it does not realise. It is not evidence that FB2-SW-SWR-000002 is met: that requirement's 10 ms comparison latency and its debounce behaviour are not established by anything listed here, and the corpus already records that the source implements no SOA debounce counter. It confers no production authority, no verification credit, and no human approval.

partial_coverage: The design's DEBOUNCING state and its 'debounce count configurable (default 2)' constraint are NOT realised in this module. soa.c contains no static variable, no counter and no debounce state at the pinned commit. The debouncing the corpus describes is the DIAG layer's occurrence counter, configured per entry in diag_cfg.c with DIAG_SEN_EVENT_50 for the cell-voltage tiers and DIAG_DELAY_200ms for the MSL tiers (diag_cfg.c:126-131). This is a different mechanism at a different layer with different parameters, and the module does not implement the design's.

The design's VIOLATION_CONFIRMED -> FAULT_TRIGGERED -> fault_request output is not an output of this module. SOA_CheckVoltages returns void. The fault request is raised downstream by BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet and BMS_IsBatterySystemStateOkay in bms.c:515-575, which poll the DIAG fatal-error link table and act on the shortest configured delay. The design's 'SOA_SYS_OUT fault_request' signal is therefore not implemented at the interface the design declares.
The design's 'violation_details' output does not exist. The detail carried out of the module is the DIAG occurrence counter, not a structured violation record.
The design's 'per-cell debounce' decision DEC-SOA-002 is not observable in this module for the same reason there is no debounce: nothing is counted per cell here.

SOA_CheckSlaveTemperatures (soa.c:353-354) exists as an empty function body carrying only a TODO. It is named here so that the record does not imply slave-temperature supervision is implemented; it is not.
implements.relationship: This function group is where FB2-SW-DSN-000002's limit-comparison and diagnosis-raising responsibilities are actually carried. The mechanism, read from the pinned source: SOA_CheckVoltages (soa.c:81-146) iterates BS_NR_OF_STRINGS and, for each string, compares maximumCellVoltage_mV against the nested thresholds BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MOL_mV, then BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_RSL_mV, then BC_VOLTAGE_MAX_MSL_mV, calling DIAG_Handler with DIAG_EVENT_NOT_OK on each crossed tier and with DIAG_EVENT_OK on each tier the value has fallen back inside; the minimum voltage is handled symmetrically against BC_VOLTAGE_MIN_MOL/RSL/MSL_mV, and the undervoltage-MSL handler's return value is captured so that a simultaneous deep-discharge crossing raises DIAG_ID_DEEP_DISCHARGE_DETECTED as well. SOA_CheckTemperatures (148-269) branches on BMS_GetCurrentFlowDirection(i_current) and compares against a DISCHARGE tier set or a CHARGE tier set accordingly, so the limit that applies depends on current direction rather than on mode alone. SOA_CheckCurrent (271-351) skips a string entirely when invalidStringCurrent[s] is non-zero, computes an absolute current, evaluates string and cell current limits per direction, and separately raises DIAG_ID_CURRENT_ON_OPEN_STRING when a current is measured on a string whose contactors are open. What is absent is any counter: the module holds no static state at all, so it cannot debounce.
